title: Speed Up on Phase Out
summary:
Speed Up on Phase Out
This week we examine the VLCC fleet with regard to the impact of regulatory phase-out of single hull tankers. The VLCC fleet size over the last 10 years has been static as shown below. This stable fleet size is a result of annual scrapping activity more or less equaling newbuilding deliveries until 2004, when scrapping activity declined significantly.

children.title: DELIVERED
children.summary: SCRAPPED Even though the VLCC fleet has stagnated numerically, double hull vessels built in the 1990s and 2000s are faster, larger, more fuel-efficient, and operate more days per year than those being scrapped. 1 Newer VLCCs are approximately 20% more productive than the vessels they are replacing.

children.title: Deliveries
children.summary: Anticipated Deliveries Removals Anticipated Removals The Erika sinking in late 1999 and the Prestige sinking in late 2003 introduced age preference into the chartering decisions of oil companies, reducing supply below physical availability and helping to cause the greatest charter rate rise in the history of tankers. The new MARPOL provision on single hull phase- out actually could have a greater impact on vessel supply than the Erika and Prestige combined.
